Title: Old English Continental Network: Collaboration, Research and Teaching [OE-CONNECT]
Description: OE-CONNECT aims to create a sustainable interdisciplinary network of researchers and teachers working on the cultural heritage of early medieval England (c. 500–1100 CE) at continental European institutions.
Institutions: Jagiellonian University in Kraków; Leiden University; University of Zurich

Title: Electronic Corpus of Anonymous Homilies in Old English [ECHOE]
Description: ECHOE is a digital text corpus currently counting 553,249 tokens in 337 manuscript versions of Old English anonymous and Wulfstanian homilies and saints’ lives edited from 60 manuscripts, version by version.
Funding: European Research Council (ERC); Alexander von Humboldt Stiftung

Title: Early Medieval English in Nineteenth-Century Europe [EMERGENCE]
Description: In the 19th century, Old English poems were claimed as cultural heritage by various non-Anglophone nations, including Scandinavians, Germans and Dutch. These competing nationalistic, cultural appropriations happened against the backdrop of a growing interest in early medieval English language and literature across the European continent. The EMERGENCE project explores this transnational reception of Old English and offers a new perspective on the 19th-century foundations of Old English Studies.

Title: Nerthus Project
Description: This project intends to contribute to the debate on the applications of large language models (LLMs) in various scientific fields, while also proposing the integration of artificial intelligence in the processing of less-documented languages. The objectives of this project are (i) to implement a language model for Old English based on a natural language processing (NLP) library adjusted for morphosyntactic annotation with Universal Dependencies (UD); and (ii) to automatically annotate a corpus of Old English prose consisting of 300,000 words with Universal Dependencies.
Funding: Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades
